and during the interview Primus found them suitably duplicitous for the task. They also had a solid employment record having worked for the Djinn Ibliss for over fifty years, whilst moonlighting as soothsayers for the Togaduine Travelling Circus. Owuo also resembled Lilith with her swarthy skin and dark hair, but her pale blue and white eyes set her apart making her a novel entity for both rituals and tourists.

On entering Lilith’s chambers, Kufia, a shaman with kinship to Baron Samedi, presented Lilith with the news of the day, namely that Primus’s lover, Boaca Baer, was with child.

Lilith was disgruntled by the revelation.
Kyrie was disgruntled by the interruption.
Primus was disgruntled that Kufia was muckraking.

And Boaca Baer was disgruntled some seven moons later at giving birth to a blob of two-hundred and sixteen conjoined humanoid, demonic cephalopods.

She was even more disgruntled twelve years after that when Primus returned, after she had raised the Nicolai, and stole his monstrous son to Irkalla for an apprenticeship.

The whole matter put Lilith in a pithy mood and made her more determined than ever to get rid of her husband, however long it took, and she was not at all happy with the presence of Nicolas, only tolerating him because Theaten was overjoyed to have a little brother.

Of course, Theaten did not meet Nicolas until Nicolas was fully grown on account of Primus not wanting to frighten him by showing him young Nicolas; the grotesque cosmic splat.

Neither Primus nor Nicolas told Theaten about the Nicolai, not because they could not trust him but because games of hide and seek offered hours of amusement at Theaten’s expense.

Scene V: The Duplicitous Baers

The 1st Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Corax Asylum, Togaduine

Two beings rode towards the gates of Corax. One was a large, heavy-set man wearing a wolf skin cloak. From his thick, tan leather pants swung a sheathed dagger, and his dunn carried a shield on his behalf. His greying beard swallowed up the fair skin beneath masking world-weary wrinkles and scars.

His partner’s appearance contrasted with his. She was stunningly swarthy with flowing locks of curly black hair that matched her eyes and she wore a shredded dress soaked in elaborate brown and blue swirls. Her tiara matched her dress, and she too carried a blade at her side.

The gates flung themselves open welcoming the duo.

They cantered across the barren grounds to the front of the asylum where they were met by two porters dressed in orange and green overalls. The young gentlemen helped the couple down and led their horses away to be fed and have their thirsts quenched.

The arched oak door of the asylum was also open, and a Nicolai dressed in black, sporting long flowing brown locks met them.
‘You must be BaerNedi, and…’ He took the woman’s hand and kissed it, ‘Banshee Baer, your beauty is only preceded by its reputation.’
Banshee Baer smiled, took a double take whilst considering the implication of his words, then smiled again,
‘And which Nicolas are you?’ She asked.
‘Nicolai-Nicolas Nachtvinsky. I am afraid Chives could not meet you. He has gone to Sapari to collect Nicolas’s new suit.’
‘That’s fine.’ Banshee nodded, ‘Will Nicolas be joining us today?’
‘Unfortunately, not, Madam, he is allegedly writing a book with Nicolai-Binky, but to be honest I suspect he is sulking in his office as yesterday’s tribute-brain upset his stomach,’ Nachtvinsky lied. ‘Trust me, you would not want to be in the same room as him right now. Archie has Ball on standby to clean up any leakage.’

Ball was Nicolas’s favourite mutant, and he kept Ball in Corax with a rag or towel attached to him so that the monstrous ball could roll around clearing up noxious messes on demand.

‘Now,’ Nachtvinsky smiled, ‘I was just in the middle of writing the Corax national anthem when Nicolai-Archie asked me to fetch you, so follow me.’
Banshee and BaerNedi followed the maestro as he hummed an awful, off-key melody to himself. They bypassed the office, which had two Nicolai standing temporarily wedged in the doorway to block their view, then walked by the banqueting hall and headed south.

After passing several doors, whose locksets offered joyous grins to welcome them, Nachtvinsky stopped at a rickety archway covered with a yellow and black plaid curtain,
‘In there,’ he gestured, ‘they are waiting for you.’

Banshee pulled the curtain aside and the rail shuddered. The two walked into the not-so-secret games room. The room matched the general damp and fungal aesthetic of the overall asylum. There were books, plates and papers strewn about the floor, some of which had their own sporous communities, and in the centre of the room an old, neglected teak table wobbled and groaned.

Four beings sat around the table playing games.

The first to speak was Nicolai-Archie. His name was not really Archie. Archie had no name as he was far too good for a proper noun. By trade he was an architect, so Nicolas called him Archie, and the Nicolai followed suit. Archie wore a splendid bright red and black, flamboyant suit covered in diamonds. His hat matched his suit and flourished with feathers. A monocle perched on his right eye,
‘Come, sit, our illustrious baers,’ he said, whilst gesturing to some empty chairs that pulled themselves out invitingly on the other side of the table.

The baers took their places at the table.

Opposite Archie slumped a masked figure wearing a burgundy and purple cloak and hood. On the table between Archie and the hooded figure sat a chessboard.
‘Elyas and I are partaking in a game of wits,’ Archie explained, ‘Elyas is losing.’
‘You’re cheating,’ Elyas replied.

This comment prompted the gentleman in the purple suit and hat, which sat next to Archie, to speak up,
‘No, Elyas, you’re cheating.’ The red-haired gentleman, Nicolai-Chester said as he pulled a deck of cards from his pocket.

Chester dealt seven cards to himself, and then seven cards to the third Nicolai at the table, Nicolai-Nicolas Remdali.

Remdali considered himself an artist and wore an oversized top hat sporting a melted pocket watch, and a suit patterned with embroidered pocket watches to match. His moustache was long and curled at the ends and he spoke with a stupid and clearly phoney accent,
‘Whata are we-a playing, mio amico?’
‘Rummy,’ Chester spat, ‘me first.’

Archie turned and looked at Chester’s cards, as he did, Elyas pinched Archie’s rook and hid it under the table.

Banshee’s eyes widened, but she said nothing about Elyas’s cheeky move, instead opting to ask,
‘Archie, Sir, I thought Elyas was banned from Corax?’
Archie turned back, looked at the board narrowing his eyes, then glared at Elyas,
‘Nicolas is indisposed today, Banshee, and what he does not know does not hurt him!’

Chester picked up a card and added his own two penny’s worth,
‘He’s got the shits.’
‘He is indisposed,’ Archie reiterated as he waved his hand towards Elyas, ‘as this necromancer will be if he does not return my rook.’
‘I don’t have your rook!’ Elyas bit back.
Archie growled and then hissed,
‘I will count to three… One.’

‘Umm,’ BaerNedi interrupted, ‘you summoned us?’
‘Si!’ Remdali replied putting down a joker for no reason in the world. Chester sighed, but said nothing, and instead laid a blank card.
‘We ‘ave a presento for you,’ Remdali continued.
‘Indeed, we do!’ Archie concurred, as Elyas put his rook on the wrong square, ‘We have a Mica.’

‘What’s a Mica?’ Banshee asked.
‘Not what, who?’ Chester replied, picking up his own blank card as Elyas moved the knight diagonally across the board.
‘Mica,’ Archie continued, ‘is a vampire, and he has been selected by Nicolas to betray Nicolas to our third Immoless.’

Chester glanced at the mirror on the wall behind Remdali, who desperately needed the ace of spades, rummaged through the pile, and took the card for himself. Archie responded by moving his king forward six spaces.

‘Do you know how to play these games?’ Banshee asked curiously.

The Nicolai and Elyas all stopped what they were doing and stared at her. They leaned forward in their chairs and drew their lips back. The candles dimmed.

Banshee let out a cough,
‘I, I was joking,’ she stuttered, ‘of course you do. I’m sorry.’
Chester grunted a single syllable indicative of a laugh, the candles glowed brightly, and the players resumed their games. Banshee tried to quell an involuntary sigh of relief,
‘Tell us about Mica.’
‘Who?’ Chester asked.
‘Mica.’
‘Who?’
Banshee looked towards Archie, who moved his bishop six steps forward and one to the left. Elyas responded with a gallant move, sacrificing his king to save the queen. The queen did not need saving and was very surprised when the king threw himself off the board and onto Chester’s messy heap of cards, which Remdali was flicking about in circles.

‘Mica,’ Archie said after an awkward silence, ‘is a vampire, and you shall take him to the Immoless. He will be her next victim. He has been supplied with enough information; tell her you found him wandering about some forest or another.’
‘We shall set this up exactly as Nicolas has advised,’ Banshee nodded reassuringly.
‘You had better,’ Chester growled. He then sniffed twice and added
‘Now, you girl, come here?’

Banshee went to stand when the curtain opened and a malnourished and blood-stained tribute with patches of her lank red-hair missing walked in. Her head hung and she looked at the floor. She shifted slowly, with a slight limp, and knelt before Chester,
‘Yes Sir?’
Chester pulled her to her feet. A long black tongue drooled from his mouth and licked her all over, then withdrew, happy with its exploration.

Chester pressed her back to her knees and whispered,
‘Fetch Mica!’
‘Yes Sir,’ the woman replied. She stood slowly, her eyes downcast, and backed out of the archway.

‘How did you know she was there?’ Banshee asked.
Chester glared at her. Archie glared at her, and both spoke at once in a low, unified voice,
‘Don’t ever question me again.’

Banshee lowered her head.
‘Forgive her,’ BaerNedi pleaded, ‘she forgets herself at times.’
Chester nodded,
‘Forgiven but not forgotten.’
Banshee shivered.

Mica arrived alone. He waited at the opened aperture until summoned by a click of Chester’s finger and thumb.
‘Buongiorno,’ Remdali said, laying two cards at once, ‘it’s-a your time. A.’
Mica bowed,
‘Am I to suffer the boiling?’
‘Si,’ Remdali replied as Chester picked up three cards, and Elyas jumped Archie’s knight with a pawn.

Mica folded his arms tightly across his body. Silence filled the room as Archie and Remdali simultaneously stared at the vampire. Chester spoke first,
‘We know what you are,’
‘Thinking,’ Archie continued, ‘fear of pain. Fear of death. Potential escape.’
‘But we promise you,’ Remdali butted in, ‘much worse awaits traitors.’
‘Even Irkalla can’t hide a traitor,’ Chester muttered.

‘I understand,’ Mica replied.
‘We can give him something to alleviate the pain,’ Banshee suggested, her head still lowered.
‘No!’ Archie and Chester snapped, ‘Bring the pain.’
‘As you wish.’

Archie added three draught pieces to the board,
‘Now, about the third Immoless. How is she?’
Banshee breathed deeply through her nose,
‘She thinks she has an alcohol problem. She is prepared for her destiny, a little bit moody about dying, but prepared.’
‘And the blackouts?’
‘They continue.’
‘Yes, they do,’ Chester leered, ‘but tell me, does she love her boyfriend?’

Banshee bit her lip hard,
‘May I speak freely, Sir?’
‘No one is stopping you,’ Chester replied, collecting all cards and shuffling them, ‘we value honesty.’
‘She feels that love is not meant for her, and that her impending death is a barricade to it.’
‘That is-a logic, not-a sentimenta-a,’ Remdali said as he pulled a piece of parchment and pencil from his suit and drew two stick people.
‘Allyra is melancholy,’ Banshee whispered, ‘it is heart-breaking to watch.’
Chester nodded,
‘We appreciate your honesty, Banshee, but you must not get attached. This attachment concerns Nicolas. She will meet Nicolas soon, and then Nicolas will be responsible for her. She will no longer be your concern, remember where your loyalties lie.’ Chester then changed the subject, ‘I think her sex addiction is more than ready for us. She has had a good tutor in that regards.’
‘Indeed,’ Banshee replied.
Chester flicked his wrist in her direction,
‘You may depart now, and don’t forget to take Mica with you.’

Banshee and BaerNedi stood, bowed to each of the players, then walked backwards through the archway taking Mica with them through the sea of wailing inmates. Their horses were waiting for them outside. Banshee took Mica on her steed, and BaerNedi led the way back to Sapari.

The two Nicolai waited until the baers had departed, stepped away from the office door, and left Nicolas to grin wildly at the wall in his own time. Nicolas found the wall less insipid than the baers, and he knew Banshee’s growing fondness for Allyra was cause for concern.

Scene VI: Confusius Maximus

The Sapari Tavern, Sapari
The 1stDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.

Allyra arrived at the Sapari Tavern just before midday. The rustic public house was quiet with just a few men sitting along the chipped, wooden bar, which ran the length of the tavern, and a few families seated quietly in the wooden booths opposite. The drink of choice, mulled cider, spread a potent ambience about the lounge to accompany the sounds of the men talking shit and laughing far too loudly. Wafts of smoke from Ashurrel leaf and cigars also stifled and stunk out the inn. Overall, the environment was a feast for the soul if the soul enjoys immense suffocation.

The owners, John and Jaeli Montgomery, were out for the day, so Allyra approached the barmaid, Charmaine. Charmaine was a small blonde lady with ridiculously large curves that seemed to have had an argument with her saucy red dress. The dress complained constantly about the poor fitting, and on occasion the laces would bust open of their own accord giving everyone an eyeful of Charmaine’s portly breasts. This embarrassed Charmaine and she would quickly try to force her flesh back into the upper corset of the gown. The men at the bar did not object to the floor show, although they often asked how she could possibly breathe. Charmaine would laugh, blow them a kiss, and continue to wear the wayward garment regardless of it inhibiting her lung capacity.

Allyra squished between two old, balding men, whose cigars needed flicking, and addressed Charmaine directly,
‘Char, has Lord Fontacue checked in?’
Charmaine, who was bored with the bar room banter looked up from her game of Solitaire,
‘‘Ello Lyra, take a seat. I will be with you in a minute.’

Allyra looked up and down the bar, and picked a depressed, three-legged stool at the far end, which offered quick and subtle access to the stairs, so that she could meet her mark without everyone pointing out what a trollop she was.

Charmaine abandoned her punters and slowly followed Allyra to the far end of the bar. Once Allyra had sat down, a difficulty given the tightness of her shiny black leather catsuit, Charmaine leaned across the bar,
‘I need to speak to you,’ she whispered, then yelled, ‘WHAT can I get you?’ To divert the unwanted attention of any nosey punters.

The men did not look up as they were too engrossed in their discussion about whether the monster of the Twin Lakes, of which there was only one lake, could travel via land to the Getsug Sea. The conversation was largely redundant as the mythical beast was known to be a freshwater monster, not a saltwater monster.

Allyra twiddled her thumbs nervously. In spite of her bravado, she was always nervous before meeting a mark due to some of the strange requirements often suggested in exchange for information. Lord Fuckwad, for example, liked to dress in a romper suit and be burped like a baby. Lord Lucien Nerison, who had once petitioned for Allyra’s hand in marriage and been rejected by her father, Tempus, insisted on the pair of them rolling around in a bath of mud whilst popping balloons, and Lord Fontacue enjoyed something he called water sports, only it did not involve the sea.

Allyra avoided alcohol before meeting a mark as she did not wish to pass out and wake up wearing a diaper and floating through the sky tied to helium balloons. She was an open-minded sex addict but floating about The Deep looking like an idiot was not in her remit.
‘Water please,’ Allyra said, ‘I woke up in the sea again. The salt is making me dry.’
Charmaine nodded,
‘Fair enough.’ She grabbed a rather grubby glass from the shelf, tipped out an errant and sadly lost slug, and poured some yellowing water into it from an even dirtier jug.

Allyra pulled her hair from her neck and tucked it back behind her ears as she had a tendency to dribble. Her dark eyes frowned at the odd looking liquid, but she had drunk worse and was thirsty. The first mouthful was a bit harsh, so she held her nose and swallowed quickly allowing the rest to glob down her throat. Charmaine faked dealing cards to her friend and continued to whisper,
‘Lord Fontacue didn’t come in. Someone else did in his place, and he is… Lyra you are in danger.’
‘I know that’ Allyra whispered, ‘I’m being sent to the Immortalis soon, so death… Danger. Goes without saying.’
Charmaine shook her head,
‘There are worse things than death. After your ‘meeting’ with… Just come and find me at The Dokeshi Carnival. I need to talk to you about Nicolas.’
‘Nicolas?’ Allyra raised an eyebrow, ‘Nicolas DeSilva?’
‘Yes, THAT Nicolas. The Electi have been lying to you. They made a pact…’

As she spoke a tall man entered the bar. He wore a red and black suit covered with diamonds, a top hat, and a monocle, and to anyone who knew anything about the Immortalis, looked a little bit like Nicolas.

Charmaine stopped talking instantly and changed the subject,
‘Room three. Up you go. Hope your meeting goes well.’
‘But’ Allyra began.
Charmaine side-eyed the dazzling figure standing perfectly still by the door,
‘Just go NOW and get your meeting over with.’

Allyra slipped off the stool and hopped up the wide wooden stairs, hoping to gain some valuable intelligence about the Immortalis. She was very well aware that the Electi had no intention of providing such information and had more heed, as priests often do, on alcohol and sex.

Room three was not the third door along the musky, scarlet carpeted corridor. Not from either end. Initially room numbers had not been used but this resulted in sexual liaisons and dalliances where there ought not to have been sexual liaisons and dalliances and caused a great deal of newsworthy scandal.

The scandal was picked up by one Nicolai-Silas Gideon Alaric Bartholomew-Crispin (with a hyphen) Ledgerly. Nicolai-Ledgerly published all the sordid details in a pamphlet entitled, Tickturdery in Sapari, the 1st Moon of 1531 Special Edition and distributed said pamphlet to every household in The Deep. Ledgerly, who did not believe in censorship, made sure that every name, connection, and sordid detail was conveyed in full and provided accompanying sketches for clarification purposes. This caused a massive surge in divorce cases and embarrassed just about everyone.

As such, in the 2nd Moon of 1531 P.V. the landlords, John and Jaeli Montgomery, contracted one Jonas Citpo of Togaduine to number the doors. They could have done it themselves, but Lord Fuckwad’s wife had insisted to Lord Fuckwad that employment should be more inclusive. Lord Fuckwad, who had to live with Lady Fuckwad, wrote to Count Tepes regarding the matter. Tepes wrote to Theaten, and Theaten, who could not make head nor tail of the letter, sent the matter directly to Nicolas.

Nicolas thought diversity in employment was a wonderful idea and sent Jonas Citpo, a blind and deaf farmer that resided near Corax, to Sapari. Nicolas was so taken with the idea of inclusivity in employment that he insisted that all public and private signs were to be constructed by Jonas, without any assistance or supportive aid. Anyone who objected would be considered rude and subsequently stoned to death in the town square stocks. Nicolas could not abide exclusivity as he considered everyone equally worthless. The numbers in the tavern were, therefore, sitting wherever they pleased. This issue was nowhere near as problematic as the horde of tourists who had been driving their carriages around in circles, following inaccurate road signs and diversions, for the better part of five years.

Allyra knocked on the door.
‘Enter,’ the voice from within growled. She turned the handle only to find the door locked,
‘Can you unlock the door please?’ Allyra asked, knocking again.
‘If you can answer a question to demonstrate your cognitive abilities.’
‘Why?’
A deafening silence followed, and Allyra knocked again.
‘Yes?’ Came the reply.
‘Open the door.’
‘If you can answer the most taxing question and prove yourself worthy, I shall endeavour to release the great portcullis.’
‘This is stupid,’ Allyra mumbled.
‘Wrong answer!’ The voice boomed, ‘Do you want to try another?’
‘Another what?’
‘Another question.’
‘You didn’t give me a question in the first place, so how can you give me another question?’
‘This too is incorrect. I can always give you more but never less!’
‘You can give less! You can give someone less attention than someone else. You can give someone less mead than someone else.’ Allyra argued to no avail.
‘You may only enter if you answer a question!’ The voice replied, aggressively.
Allyra sighed wilfully loudly and leaned against the door,
‘Fine, ask a question.’

A short silence followed, then the voice returned,
‘What waves, then abates, then waves, then abates, then waves, then…?’
Allyra considered the question very briefly then yelled through the chunk of wood,
‘I presume you mean the sea, but it ebbs and flows.’
‘Next question,’ the voice continued, ‘what is the distance between two points?’
‘Which two points?’ Allyra asked, not really expecting a sensible response.
‘Any two!’
Allyra rolled her eyes,
‘Do you want sex or not?’
Another short silence followed, then the click of the lock rang out. Allyra turned the handle, pushed the door, and entered.

The room was sparse comprising of a small double bed with yellow and black plaid sheets, a bedside table hugging an oil lamp, and a tiny window.

Allyra’s suitor sat on the bed wearing a black and green suit that covered his entire body, and a mask that covered his entire head. Both suit and mask were embossed with gold question marks. Allyra bit her cheek so as not to laugh,
‘Did you come from a fancy dress party?’
‘No, Madam, I came from Togaduine,’ the being replied in a gruff voice with a hint of an accent Allyra could not place.
‘Where, may I ask, is Lord Fontacue?’
The man laid back on the bed and folded his arms behind his head,
‘Which question would you like me to answer first?’
‘What?’ Allyra asked, releasing an exacerbated breath.
The bizarre costumed being raised one leg,
‘You asked if you may ask, and then you asked about the whereabouts of Lord Fontacue, which question shall I answer?’
‘Where is Lord Fontacue?’ Allyra snapped, her patience waning.

The leg lowered and a silly speech began,
‘Lord Fontacue, alas, is with us no more. He was riding his donkey, Jackass, late at night. A great rider he was, for riding was not his problem. No. The meteor was the problem. It ricocheted from the sky after a tiresome journey and fell squarely on Lord Fontacue’s head. Sadly, neither Lord Fontacue, nor his steed, nor the milkmaid he was intending to ride made it. A tale of such bittersweet sorrow. Of course, Mrs Fontacue is quite pleased with the insurance payouts. It puts me in mind of the story of the old wars between the snakes and the bees. Terrible thing. Would you like me to tell you about it?’
Allyra plonked herself on the bed next to her strange companion,
‘No!’

‘‘Twas the long hot summer somewhere in the depths of the eighth century that the wasps were overcome by loneliness. A sad time. So many drones working away with no queen. Very sad they were, when the king of the wasps, King George Edward Theobold Wallace McVite McCallanus Esquire and Sons, sought the love of a queen. They ventured forth and what did they find?’
‘Bullshit?’ Allyra asked.
‘No, Madam, they found the queen of the mambas. Treacherous she was. Spiteful. They all fell in love with her despite her RUDENESS and passive hostility and took her to their nest. She was very much in love with all of them, even though she denied it…’

Allyra looked at her watch, but this did not discourage her suitor who carried on regardless,
‘And the queen of the bees got jealous. Do you know what happened next?’
‘I have a date with my boyfriend later,’ Allyra complained, trying to hurry the weirdo along.
‘That is incorrect. The queen of the mambas ate the queen of the bees and then the wasps ate the skin of the queen of the mambas, shedding it for her,

text:
Synagogue of Satan (Greek: συναγωγή τοῦ Σατανᾶ, romanized: synagōgḗ toũ Satanã) is a phrase from Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 in which Jesus refers to a group persecuting the church, falsely claiming to be Jews. The exact meaning of who the text is referring to is unclear, but there are two prevailing views: either unbelieving Jews who did not recognize Jesus as a Messiah, or Christians who have integrated into practices of the surrounding culture. While it can be antisemitic if taken out of context, John of Patmos, the author of Revelation was likely Jewish and the use of the word "Jew" in Revelation is consistently positive.

Later Church Fathers used the same phrase or similar in polemical writings warning against Jews infiltrating the church, or Christians attending synagogue. During the Reformation, the phrase was used in polemics against the Catholic Church. The Catholic Church instead used the phrase as a descriptor of both the enemies of the church and Freemasonry.

In the modern era, the verses have been used to justify antisemitism by conspiracy theorists and followers of Christian Identity who believe the Serpent seed doctrine that Jews are the literal descendants of Satan. It is also used more generally as a pejorative of any non-Christian religious practices considered to be associated with idolatry or the devil.

Origin in Revelation
In the New Testament book of Revelation, in the letters to the early Christian churches of Smyrna and Philadelphia in Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the author quotes Jesus as speaking of the Synagogue of Satan, in each case referring to a group persecuting the church "who say they are Jews and are not".[1]

And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: "The words of the first and the last, who died and came to life. I know your tribulation and your poverty (but you are rich) and the slander of those who say that they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan."

— Revelation 2:8–9 (ESV)
And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write... "I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut. I know that you have but little power, and yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name. Behold, I will make those of the synagogue of Satan who say that they are Jews and are not, but lie—behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will learn that I have loved you."

— Revelation 3:7–9 (ESV)
While the phrase "synagogue of Satan" is a negative term, the precise meaning in the text is uncertain. The association of Jews with Satan begins not in Revelation, but in the Gospel of John.[2] In John 8:44, Jesus charges the Jewish authorities as being of the devil.[3] Biblical scholar Stefan Schreiber draws parallels from this passage, Rev 2:9, 3:9, and Acts: "The devil as the opponent per se functions as a paradigm of the opposing Jewish majority refusing to accept Christ; so in John 8:44, the Jewish authorities are charged with having the devil as their father, and in Rev 2:9, 3:9, the Jewish communities in Asia Minor are dismissed as 'synagogue of Satan'. An opponent of the Christian mission from outside is called 'son of the devil' in Acts 13:10".[4]

There are two prevailing views of who is being referred to in this passage. The dominant view that it refers to unbelieving Jews, or those Jews who do not recognize Christ as Messiah.[5][6] The Oxford Handbook of the Book of Revelation summarizes this as "hostile ethnic Jews... no longer belong to the true community of God, the in-group, but to the 'synagogue of Satan,' the out-group. Thus, the true people of God are no longer 'those who say that they are Jews' but those who worship the almighty God as revealed in the Lamb that was slain".[7] New Testament scholar James Resseguie points out that according to the argument of various scholars supporting this view, Jews and Christians are locked in intense conflict in the regions to which the letters are addressed, and since Jews do not follow the Lamb, they belong, according to the author of Revelation, to the congregation of Satan.[8]: 88–89 

The alternative view is that this phrasing refers to heretical Christians following other doctrines such as the Nicolaitans or Jezebel.[5][6] Resseguie describes them as Christians who have integrated into the practices of the surrounding culture, pointing out that while the phrasing may seem antisemitic if taken out of context, the author of Revelation is likely Jewish and use of the word "Jew" in the book is consistently positive.[8]: 89 

Qumran community
Language similar to the "synagogue of Satan" phrasing in Revelation appears in the Dead Sea Scrolls, written by the Qumran community that viewed the rest of Judaism as apostate, calling its persecutors "the lot of Belial" (Satan).[9] The Community Rule uses "the lot of Belial" as a contrast to righteous community members. Through sin, humans place themselves in with Belial's lot.[10] This presents a cosmic dualism in which humans are either part of the light or part of the darkness, the lot of God or the lot of Belial.[11]

Post-Nicene polemics
During the Post-Nicene period, the exact phrasing from Revelation as well as similarly themed versions of it were used in various adversus judaeos (against the Jews) polemical writings addressing ongoing conflicts between Christians and Jews. While Jerome was the only Early Church Father to use the exact term "synagogue of Satan" as a pejorative,[12] other Post-Nicene Fathers such as Ambrose of Milan and John Chrysostom wrote on similarly phrased themes.

Jerome
Jerome used the "synagogue of Satan" phrasing as a polemic in his correspondence with Augustine of Hippo.[13]

If, however, there is for us no alternative but to receive the Jews into the Church, along with the usages prescribed by their law; if, in short, it shall be declared lawful for them to continue in the Churches of Christ what they have been accustomed to practise in the synagogues of Satan, I will tell you my opinion of the matter: they will not become Christians, but they will make us Jews.

— Jerome, Letters of St. Augustine, LXXV
Jerome also used the phrase in his letter to Pammachius and Oceanus, arguing that the Jews "persecute our Lord Jesus Christ in the synagogues of Satan".[14] Additionally, he used the similar phrase "synagogue of antichrist" in his polemical writing.[12]

Augustine
In addition to the uses by Jerome, the phrase was used by Augustine in at least one clear related usage. In On Baptism, Augustine engages a statement from the African bishop Rogatianus of Nova: "Christ established the Church, the devil heresy: how can the synagogue of Satan have the baptism of Christ?"[14]

John Chrysostom
Although not using the precise phrase "synagogue of Satan", John Chrysostom developed similar polemical themes in Adversus Judaeos, a series of sermons given in Antioch in 387 specifically to Christians who were attending synagogue services, which Chrysostom equated to blasphemy.[15] In the first of these sermons, Chrysostom called the synagogue a "dwelling of demons".[16]

But when God abandons a people, what hope of salvation is left? When God abandons a place, that place becomes the dwelling of demons.

— John Chrysostom, Adversus Judaeos, 1.3
Chrysostom further attests that the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple was an act of God's wrath and that although there are holy books in the synagogue, that does not make it holy.[15]

Ambrose
Ambrose was another Post-Nicene writer who developed adversus judaeos themes. He called the synagogue "a place of unbelief, a house of impiety, a shelter of madness, which God himself condemned".[17][18] In his commentary on the Gospel of Luke, Ambrose associated the synagogue with demon possession, asking, "Wasn't it the Jewish people in the synagogue who are possessed by the unclean spirit of demons?"[19]: 32 

Dioscorus
American theologian William Hatch identified a lost work on Pope Dioscorus I of Alexandria that also uses the phrase "synagogue of Satan".[20]

He was summoned to the synagogue of Satan. When he came in to that place, he saw many more multitudes. On account of this he said, "What deficiency (is there) which the orthodox faith lacks? " They said to him thus: "In the counsel of the king the multitudes have been assembled to pervert the faith." At once he said to them, "If these numerous multitudes have been assembled concerning Jesus Christ, I will sit down and speak in it that which Christ has spoken to my mouth. But I ought to confess the orthodox faith and say thus: Lord Jesus, Emmanuel, our God, has never been divided in all his works; but (he is) one only Lord, one only nature; he has one only will; and the deity has united with the humanity as the soul unites with the flesh. This is my declaration and my confession, - I the least, Dioscorus, the poor.

— Dioscorus
Hatch believed the "synagogue of Satan" here refers to the Council of Chalcedon, which Dioscorus attended in 451 and from which he was deposed and exiled for his miaphysitism.[20]

Protestant Reformation
During the Reformation, the phrase shifted from polemics against Jews to those against the Catholic Church and its offices. In Actes and Monuments, John Foxe refers to the Roman Catholic Church as the synagogue of Satan.[21] Jan Hus used the term in reference to cardinals claiming to be vicars of Christ.[22] In similar fashion, John Stilman, who was tried before the bishop of London in 1518 said the College of Cardinals were Antichrist and "all other inferior prelates and priests are the synagogue of Satan".[23] In Truth's Triumph over Trent, a work comparing Protestantism and the Catholic Church, Puritan theologian Henry Burton referred to the Catholic Church as the apostate synagogue of Antichrist.[24][25]

Catholic Church
Pope Pius IX used the phrase in multiple instances to describe different things. In 1864, in his Syllabus of Errors, he wrote against the secularizing tendencies of the modern world as "a war ... waged against the Catholic Church", adding in a postscript that this served to strengthen "the synagogue of Satan, which gathers its troops against the Church of Christ".[19]: 132 

Later, in the encyclical Etsi multa, in 1873, Pius refers to Freemasonry as "the synagogue of Satan". The term describes groups that teach heresy under the guise of orthodoxy.[26]

Pope Pius IX was not the only pope to use the synagogue of Satan imagery to describe Freemasonry. Pope Leo XIII identified masonic lodges as the "kingdom of Satan" in an 1884 encyclical Humanum genus.[27]

In 1893, Johann Gabriel Leon Luis Meurin wrote La Franc-maçonnerie: Synagogue De Satin (Freemasonry: Synagogue of Satan).[27][28] Meurin's work described the character of Freemasonry as Jewish, antisocietal, and satanic. It was illustrated with charts and diagrams, giving it the appearance of a scientific approach. Its main idea was that the "Jewish Kabbalah" was the philosophical basis for Freemasonry.[29]

Conspiracy theories
Illuminati conspiracy
William Guy Carr, who advanced the conspiracy theory that world affairs were controlled by the Illuminati and international bankers, often wrote in his books about a Luciferian conspiracy he attributed to the synagogue of Satan. In his book, Satan, Prince of this World, Carr claimed this was not a reference to Judaism: "I wish to make it clearly and emphatically known that I do not believe the Synagogue of Satan (S.O.S.) is Jewish, but, as Christ told us for a definite purpose, it is comprised of 'I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.'"[30]

Further, Carr stated that the purpose of the Bible's Old Testament was to describe how Satan had become prince of this world and how "the synagogue of Satan was established on this earth" to thwart God's will.[31]: 128 However, Carr's book Pawns in the Game, relying on work by Nesta Helen Webster, claimed the Illuminati had been founded by Jewish conspirators as a plot for world domination, calling this cabal a synagogue of Satan that was comprised of Jews "who had literally 'Sold their souls to the devil"'.[32]

Carr's books had an influence on American right-wing anti-communists like Robert W. Welch Jr., who used Carr's Illuminati theme in the American Opinion magazine distributed by the John Birch Society. Welch, however, was careful to remove terms like "synagogue of Satan", "Jewish influence", or "international bankers". Instead, Welch made the Illuminati a "cult of Satanism", comparing it to communism.[31]: 132 

The Illuminati conspiracy theory was later mainstreamed into religious circles by Pat Brooks, who authored a number of anti-occult books.[31]: 140 Brooks went beyond early modern distortions that Jewish cabalism was a form of occultism and overtly declared that the entire tradition of Judaism was a synagogue of Satan.[31]: 141–142 

RiverCrest Publishing, which publishes works by Texe Marrs, published a book by Andrew Carrington Hitchcock titled "The Synagogue of Satan" in which Hitchcock combines the Khazar hypothesis of Ashkenazi ancestry, the New World Order conspiracy theory, the Illuminati conspiracy theory all as part of an international Jewish conspiracy.[33][34]

Christian Identity
The 20th-century ideology of Christian Identity uses the "synagogue of Satan" of Revelation and Jesus's words in the Gospel of John to the Pharisees that they are "of their father the devil" to support their serpent seed teaching that Jews are the literal descendants of Satan.[35] In an early version of this teaching, one Identity author published a 1944 pamphlet titled The Morning Cometh that examines the teachings of Ethel Bristowe in her work Sargon the Magnificent (1927) and concludes that Cain (Sargon) is the founder of the synagogue of Satan and the father of the Jewish race.[35]: 175–176 

Doctrinally, the dual seedline teaching places Jews in conflict with the Anglo-Saxon race, a cosmic dualism of good versus evil in which Adam's seed is at war with the seed of the devil. In this teaching, Jews are not the true Israelites, and through their association with the synagogue of Satan, have deceived the Anglo-Saxons of their true identity, but failed to take away the Anglo-Saxons' covenant relationship with God as his people.[36]: 2 

Modern uses
Billy Graham used the phrase "synagogue of Satan" to refer to "one of two types of Jews" in a private 1973 White House conversation with President Richard Nixon.[37][38] In the conversation, Graham said these enemies of society "have a strange brilliance about them. They're smart. And they are energized by supernatural power".[32] When tapes of the conversation were released many years later, Graham apologized for what were deemed by many to be antisemitic remarks.[39]

Louis Farrakhan regularly uses the term in referring to Jews as the source of the world's problems. Addressing a Nation of Islam congregation in Detroit in 2016, he said that the synagogue of Satan had "mastered civilization now, but they've mastered it in evil".[40]

Christian nationalism
At the 2024 Republican National Convention where Christian nationalism was a strong theme, California Republican delegate Harmeet Dhillon, a Sikh, delivered the closing prayer in Punjabi which set off a firestorm of social media criticism. Gab CEO Andrew Torba commented that there can be "no tolerance for pagan false gods and the synagogue of Satan".[32]

Bêl (/ˈbeɪl/; from Akkadian: bēlu) is a title signifying 'lord' or 'master' applied to various gods in the Mesopotamian religion of Akkad, Assyria, and Babylonia. The feminine form is Bêlit ('Lady, Mistress') in Akkadian. Bel is represented in Greek as Belos and in Latin as Belus. Belit appears in Greek form as Beltis (Βελτις). Linguistically, Bel is an East Semitic form cognate with the Northwest Semitic Baal with the same meaning.

Bel was especially used for the Babylonian god Marduk in Assyrian and neo-Babylonian personal names or mentioned in inscriptions in a Mesopotamian context. Similarly, Bêlit mostly refers to Marduk's spouse Sarpanit. Marduk's mother, the Sumerian goddess often referred to in the Sumerian language as Ninhursag, Damkina, and Ninmah, was often known as Belit-ili ('Lady of the Gods') in Akkadian.

Other gods called "Lord" were sometimes identified totally or in part with Bel Marduk. The god Malak-bel of Palmyra is an example, attested as a messenger of Bel but existing as a deity separate to Bel/Marduk. Similarly, Zeus Belus mentioned by Sanchuniathon as born to Cronus/El in Peraea is unlikely to be Marduk. Early translators of Akkadian believed that the ideogram for the god called Enlil in Sumerian was to be read as Bel in Akkadian. Current scholarship holds this as incorrect, but Bel is used in referring to Enlil in older translations and discussions.[1]

In Mandaean cosmology, the name for Jupiter is Bil (ࡁࡉࡋ), which is derived from the name Bel.[2]

Bel of Palmyra, Syria
A god named Bel was the chief-god of Palmyra, Syria in pre-Hellenistic times; the deity was worshipped alongside the gods Aglibol and Yarhibol.[3] He was originally known as Bol,[4] after the Northwestern Semitic word Ba'al[5] (usually used to refer to the god Hadad), until the cult of Bel-Marduk spread to Palmyra; by 213 BC, Bol was renamed to Bel.[4] The Temple of Bel in Palmrya, Syria was dedicated to this god. The temple has since been destroyed by ISIS.[6]

What should we learn from the golden calf incident in Exodus 32?
Answer

The story of the golden calf is found in Exodus 32:1–6. The children of Israel had been in bondage in Egypt for over 400 years (Genesis 15:13; Acts 7:6). God called Moses, the deliverer, and told him that He had heard their cries and was about to deliver them (Exodus 3:6–8). During their time in Egypt, the Israelites had apparently begun to doubt the existence of the God their fathers worshiped (Exodus 3:13). To help Moses prove the existence and power of God, he was given a number of miraculous signs to help the Israelites believe. After all of these miracles were done, including the ten plagues on the Egyptians, the Israelites came out of Egypt with a renewed belief in the God of their fathers. They passed through the Red Sea on dry land, while the Egyptian army was drowned, and they were brought to the mountain of God to receive His laws.

The people of the Middle East were very religious, but they also worshiped many gods. The ten plagues God brought on the Egyptians were judgments against specific gods they worshiped and showed that the Lord was greater than all of them. Even Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, who was the priest of Midian and a worshiper of the true God, was impacted by the religious pluralism of the people around him. When Moses and the people arrived at Mount Sinai, and Jethro heard of all God’s works, he replied, “Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, because in this affair they dealt arrogantly with the people” (Exodus 18:11). When God gave His laws to the Israelites, He began by addressing this religious pluralism. “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me. You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me” (Exodus 20:2–5).

While Moses was up on the mountain receiving God’s laws, the people were getting anxious down on the plain. Moses spent forty days (Exodus 24:18) up on the mountain with God, and by the end of that time, the people were beginning to think Moses had died or left them. The people urged Aaron, their temporary leader, to make gods for them to follow. Since they were accustomed to having visual representations of gods, this was the natural (but sinful) result of their thinking. Aaron took their gold earrings, which they had brought from Egypt, and melted them down to make a golden idol. The idol he crafted for them was a calf, but Aaron maintained the name of the Lord in connection with it (Exodus 32:5). He was merging the pagan practices they were familiar with and the worship of the God they were just beginning to be re-acquainted with. After Aaron fashioned the gold into a calf, the people said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt” (Exodus 32:4). The people offered sacrifices and then engaged in pagan rituals, including orgies (Exodus 32:25) to worship this new god.

Why did Aaron do this? Scripture doesn’t give us the full answer, but we can put certain clues together and get a fairly good picture. First, the people’s long familiarity with idol worship would incline them to follow that method in the absence of clear direction otherwise. Second, they were already in the habit of merging their beliefs with those of the people around them, a practice that would continue to plague them throughout the kingdom years. Third, Aaron was faced with an unruly crowd that placed a demand on him. The solution of making an idol seemed reasonable.

Why did he choose a calf/bull? His lame excuse to Moses—“It just came out of the fire like this!” Exodus 32:24)—was just a feeble attempt to dodge blame. He fashioned it with a graving tool (Exodus 32:4) and took great care to form it that way. Some have tried to show that the BULL represented one of the gods of Egypt, but that doesn’t fit the text, because Aaron called a feast to the Lord (Yahweh) and said that it was the god(s) which brought them out of the land of Egypt. The bull was a symbol of strength and fertility, and the people were already familiar with bull gods from Egypt. Bulls were also typical animals of sacrifice, so to use their image as a symbol of the god being worshiped was a natural connection. Aaron’s bull was a mixture of the powerful God who delivered the people through mighty works and the pagan methods of worship that were borrowed from the people around them.

text:
❤️ PHYSICAL HEALING
EIGHT PEOPLE WHO NEED OUR PRAYERS
November 19, 2026

"The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit." — Psalm 34:18 (NIV)

1. MADDOX — CHILDHOOD LEUKEMIA

Eight-year-old Maddox was diagnosed with aggressive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in January 2025. His childhood was interrupted by chemotherapy, hospital visits, and the uncertainty of cancer. In 2026, he celebrated returning to baseball.

PRAYER: Heavenly Father, continue restoring Maddox's health. Protect him from complications and strengthen his growing body. Give his parents peace when memories of treatment awaken their fears. May his childhood be filled with laughter, friendships, and beautiful ordinary days.

2. MARIELLA — DEVASTATING BURN INJURIES

Three-year-old Mariella suffered severe burns covering approximately 65–70% of her body. Her recovery required specialized treatment at Shriners Children's Northern California. By November 2026, her family could celebrate a thriving, active little girl.

PRAYER: Lord Jesus, continue healing Mariella's skin and strengthening her body. Ease any discomfort and protect her future development. Surround her family with encouragement. Let her grow up knowing that her scars never diminish her beauty or worth.

3. MATT WEZEMAN — HEART ATTACK SURVIVOR

Matt, a Grand Rapids resident, experienced a heart attack in March 2025 after symptoms he initially mistook for heartburn. He drove himself to the emergency department, where his life-threatening condition was recognized.

PRAYER: Father, preserve Matt's heart and give him strength for healthy years ahead. Remove the shadow of fear that can follow a cardiac emergency. Bless those who live alone and may not recognize the warning signs of serious illness.

4. JENNIFER — KIDNEY FAILURE AND TRANSPLANTS

Jennifer's struggle with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis has involved dialysis and multiple kidney transplants. Her experience reveals how exhausting it can be to depend on lifesaving medical treatment year after year.

PRAYER: Merciful Father, protect Jennifer's health and sustain her courage. Bless the doctors caring for her kidneys and every person awaiting a transplant. Give strength to exhausted families and compassion to those who can become living donors.

5. ERMA — CHILDHOOD NEUROBLASTOMA

Young Erma's family entered the frightening world of childhood cancer treatment in 2025. At St. Jude, her parents found ways to preserve celebrations, creativity, and childhood joy during an enormously difficult season.

PRAYER: Jesus, bless Erma with health, healing, and years of wonderful discoveries. Strengthen her parents when their hearts become weary. Let every hospital room become a place where compassion, tenderness, and hope are never absent.

6. HEATHER BARDELEBEN — HEART ATTACKS AND CARDIAC ARREST

Heather survived two heart attacks and six cardiac arrests after chest symptoms had previously been attributed to other causes. Her story illustrates the importance of listening carefully when someone says something is wrong.

PRAYER: Heavenly Father, sustain Heather's heart and strengthen her future. Give medical professionals discernment, humility, and attentive compassion. Protect patients whose suffering is misunderstood or dismissed.

7. ARANTZA — CHILDHOOD BURN RECOVERY

Arantza suffered serious burn injuries following an accident in Mexico in December 2025. Her mother described how specialized treatment helped restore her daughter's health and mobility.

PRAYER: Lord Jesus, restore Arantza's strength and freedom of movement. Bring healing to painful memories as well as physical injuries. Bless her mother with peace, and let the years ahead contain more joyful moments than fearful ones.

8. AAMIR — CHILDHOOD BLOOD CANCER

Aamir was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia and entered a lengthy course of chemotherapy at St. Jude. His family faced the emotional demands of watching their child undergo treatment.

PRAYER: Father, strengthen Aamir through every stage of treatment and recovery. Protect his immune system, comfort him during difficult procedures, and give his family endurance. Let him experience the simple happiness every child deserves.

❤️ A PRAYER FOR ALL WHO ARE SUFFERING

Heavenly Father,

Tonight we remember the people whose suffering rarely makes headlines.

The child frightened by another needle.

The mother silently crying in a hospital corridor.

The father wondering whether he will work again.

The elderly widow enduring pain without anyone beside her.

The person who cannot afford the treatment that might restore their health.

Lord, You know their names.

You see what medical records cannot describe: the loneliness, the interrupted dreams, the financial burdens, and the courage required simply to face another morning.

We believe You are able to heal. We ask for restoration, relief, skilled medical care, and unexpected breakthroughs.

And while we wait, teach us that compassion is more than a feeling. It becomes visible when someone visits, provides a meal, pays a bill, offers transportation, or refuses to let a suffering neighbor face hardship alone.

May our prayers become acts of love.

In the powerful and merciful name of Jesus Christ,

Amen.

text:
Incident Report: Metro City Zoo
Cincinnati, OH.  
Date: 19 November 2026
Time: 11:47 AM
Location: Asian Elephant exhibit, public viewing area
Reported by: Keeper Luis Ortega
Severity: High (animal fatality; no human injuries)

(Event)

A child threw a baseball cap into the elephant enclosure. One of the elephants ingested the hat. The animal later died from internal obstruction. Visitor Cinzy Alvarez (age 9) was present with her mother and witnessed the events.

(Incident Summary)
Cinzy and her mother were standing at the front railing of the elephant yard. A boy approximately 11 years old, standing a few feet away, was arguing with his older brother. In frustration he yanked off his blue baseball cap and threw it over the barrier into the enclosure.

The youngest elephant, a 6-year-old female named Nia, walked over, picked the hat up with her trunk, and put it in her mouth. Keepers immediately radioed for help and tried to call her back with food, but she swallowed most of the cap before they could reach the gate.

Cinzy began crying and telling the keepers what she had seen. Her mother held her while security approached the boys. The older brother said the younger one “just got mad and threw it.”

Nia was isolated for veterinary care. Despite emergency treatment, she died that evening from a blockage in her digestive tract caused by the hat and its plastic brim. The other elephants in the herd showed signs of distress but remained unharmed.

(Immediate Actions)
•  Enclosure closed to the public for the rest of the day.
•  Police and animal-control officers took statements from the boys, their parents, and Cinzy’s mother.

•  Cinzy was offered water and a quiet room while her mother spoke with staff. She kept repeating that the elephant “just wanted to play with it.”
•  All remaining elephants were monitored overnight.

(Follow-up)
The family of the boy who threw the hat is being cited for violating zoo rules and endangering an animal. The zoo is reviewing barrier height and adding clearer warning signs. A full necropsy confirmed the hat as the cause of death.

Cinzy left with her mother just after noon. She refused the free stuffed animal offered at the gate.

Rest In Peace, Nia.   Such a sad incident.

A reporter who shouted a question at a gathering of world leaders in China was barred from covering the main event: the Trilateral Summit. Bloomberg TV journalist Annmarie Hordern was blocked from a key event by Chinese officials as what many view as retribution for having shouted a question in a way that the government considered rude. Hordern was then barred from Thursday's trilateral meeting among President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. She had asked President Trump if former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the United States. A White House official said the Chinese insisted the reporter not be allowed in despite the White House having pushed for admission.

A computer network used by the National Security Agency was still down on Thursday.. and that forced a number of employees to work from home for a third day. The network first went down on Tuesday because of a technical issue encountered during routine maintenance. Federal officials insist the outage was not caused by a cyber attack.

Third time's the charm? Ukraine has struck the bridge that links Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week and that has forced train service across it.. to grind to a halt. The third attack happened just before President Vladimir Putin was to meet with President Trump and China's President Xi Jinping. The timing of Ukraine‘s attacks on Europe's longest bridge.. and a prize of the Russian president.. was challenging for Moscow as Putin took part in the historic Trilateral Summit in China.

Her story had many Americans hoping, but sadly , the 9 year old hippo named Fiona.. died today. The hippo ate a hat that someone threw into her enclosure at the Cincinati Zoo.  Veterinarians watched over the animal 'round the clock.. hoping she would pass the object on her own. The hippo captured hearts after being born six weeks premature and requiring constant care. Fiona was not able to undergo surgery because of her size. A spokesperson for the Cincinnati Zoo said its staff members were crushed by the news.

text:
📊 DAILY MARKET VIEW | NOV 20, 2026

Crypto infrastructure keeps advancing, but market appetite is moving in the opposite direction. Stablecoin supply and institutional ETF flows remain weak, while another broad selloff hits U.S. equities.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
MARKET REGIME
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛡️ DEFENSIVE

BTC and ETH are both down around 9% over seven days. Extreme fear, falling stablecoin market capitalization, recent ETF withdrawals and weakness in U.S. equities point to limited risk appetite. This is a defensive environment, not confirmed evidence of a market bottom.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
TOP NEWS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Sky faces heavy USDC withdrawals after an illicit-finance report
An Inca Digital investigation identified $518M in historical transactions involving illicit-linked wallets through Sky’s Peg Stability Module, including $101.9M attributed to North Korean actors. CoinDesk later reported that more than $1.5B in USDC had left the facility. USDS remained close to its $1 peg. A large holder’s wallet was linked onchain to Poloniex, but that does not prove the exchange directed the withdrawals.
→ The concern is reserve liquidity and concentrated redemptions, not a confirmed stablecoin depeg. The $518M figure describes historical activity, not a new one-day theft.

2. U.S. stocks record a sixth consecutive daily decline
The S&P 500 fell 2% to 7,175.83, its longest losing streak since 2024. The Dow dropped 2.2% and the Nasdaq lost 2.3%, with more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks closing lower as AI-related shares weakened.
→ Broad equity weakness adds to the defensive backdrop for risk-sensitive markets, including crypto.

3. New analysis details the $3.4M exploit of  Ethereum’s sBOLD vault
K3 Capital’s sBOLD vault was drained of approximately $3.4M in about eight minutes on Nov 18. Onchain analysis published Nov 19 found that Ethereum block builders received about $1.78M in payments as bots competed to have exploit transactions processed first. These payments are not confirmed net profits.
→ The incident shows how transaction ordering can influence who captures value during an exploit. The exact link to a previously audited vulnerability remains unclear.

4. CFTC chair outlines a possible route for onchain derivatives venues in the U.S.
Chair Michael Selig said onchain venues seeking to offer derivatives to U.S. retail users would need to register as an exchange or partner with a registered one. The comments were reported from an interview, not issued as a new rule or approval for Hyperliquid.
→ U.S. access may be possible, but regulatory compliance remains a condition rather than an automatic green light.

5. IOSCO warns financial markets to prepare for quantum-computing risks
The global securities regulator, representing more than 130 jurisdictions, warned that sufficiently powerful quantum computers could threaten secure communications and other critical financial functions within five years. Blockchain networks may face a harder transition because upgrades require coordination across decentralized systems.
→ This is a long-term security and migration challenge, not evidence that current blockchains have already been compromised.

6. Singapore advances tokenized financial settlement
MAS announced the issuance of S$100M (about $77.5M) in tokenized four-week bills, settled using wholesale central bank digital currency. Separately, Ant International launched a protocol under MAS’ BLOOM initiative, with pilot transactions involving DBS and Franklin Templeton to connect tokenized deposits and money-market funds.
→ Institutions are testing blockchain for real financial settlement, although this does not imply immediate new demand for crypto assets.

7. 1inch adds Hyperliquid perpetual futures to its platform
Users of 1inch’s website and Android wallet can access Hyperliquid perpetual futures, including opening long and short positions and funding trades through the 1inch interface.
→ This expands distribution for onchain derivatives, but greater access to leverage is not the same as stronger spot-market demand.

8. Gold hits a 14-month low as rate expectations rise
Spot gold fell 1.3% to $3,674.13 per ounce on Nov 19, after touching $3,667.19, its lowest level since September 2025. A stronger U.S. dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase weighed on prices.
→ Higher interest-rate expectations remain a headwind for non-yielding assets such as gold.

9. Oil balances Strait of Hormuz risks against supply concerns
WTI settled at $83.21, down 0.06% and its lowest level since Aug 26. Brent settled at $91.98. Iran’s navy claimed two tankers had hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, but Reuters could not independently verify the report. Supply-surplus expectations and rising U.S. inventories also weighed on prices.
→ Geopolitical supply risks remain present, but the oil market is still weighing them against the possibility of ample supply.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE MORNING TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The key contrast today is between infrastructure development and actual market appetite. Singapore is testing tokenized financial settlement, while 1inch is widening access to onchain derivatives. Yet BTC and ETH remain down around 9% over seven days, stablecoin market capitalization has contracted, and sentiment is still deep in Extreme Fear.

The latest completed U.S. ETF session, Nov 18, recorded $306.5M in net outflows from Bitcoin funds and $39.8M from Ethereum funds. Nov 19 data was incomplete at the cutoff. CoinGlass also recorded about $169.6M in BTC futures liquidations over 24 hours, including $134.2M from long positions, while open interest fell 0.56%. That combination is consistent with leverage being unwound, although it does not by itself explain the entire price decline.

Stablecoin market capitalization measures aggregate token supply, not cash immediately available to buy crypto. Still, its contraction alongside ETF outflows and long liquidations does not yet show a convincing return of demand.

→ The industry can keep building while market capital and risk appetite move in the opposite direction.

What would convince you first that risk appetite is returning: sustained ETF inflows, stablecoin supply stabilizing, or stronger spot buying?

text:
Fourth Circuit backs Maryland’s authority to pursue Kalshi over unlicensed sports wagers

The Fourth Circuit ruled that Kalshi cannot prevent Maryland gaming regulators from pursuing action over sports wagers the company offered without a state license. The decision permits Maryland to continue enforcing its sports-wagering laws as Kalshi’s lawsuit against the state remains in progress. It upheld a district-court decision that had rejected Kalshi’s request for an injunction. That outcome removes the immediate injunction Kalshi sought against Maryland’s effort, but the ruling does not decide the underlying lawsuit. Nor does the decision establish that Maryland has taken further enforcement steps: the state has not said whether it will do so.

The dispute began when Maryland regulators sent Kalshi a cease-and-desist letter. The letter alleged that Kalshi was offering sports wagering illegally because it lacked a Maryland license. Kalshi argued that federal oversight by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, or CFTC, takes precedence over state gambling rules for its sports event contracts. The CFTC has backed the position that event contracts offered on prediction markets fall within its exclusive jurisdiction. The appeals court’s decision concerns whether Maryland may keep pursuing its laws during the lawsuit; it does not resolve the parties’ full dispute about the contracts.

Two members of the panel, Judges Roger Gregory and Stephanie Thacker, agreed Kalshi had not established a basis for an injunction. Their agreement on the result rested on different legal reasoning, so the decision did not produce a single shared rationale from both judges. Gregory wrote that Congress had not unmistakably taken away the states’ traditional power to regulate gambling. Thacker instead reasoned that sports event contracts are not swaps under federal commodities law and therefore do not come within the CFTC’s exclusive authority. Both opinions supported denying Kalshi an injunction, but they addressed different aspects of the relationship between federal commodities law and state gambling regulation.

Judge DeAndrea Benjamin dissented from the panel’s decision. She reasoned that the contracts are swaps and therefore subject to exclusive federal regulation. Her view differs from Thacker’s conclusion that these sports contracts are not swaps, and from Gregory’s focus on whether Congress clearly displaced state authority. The result therefore leaves the panel divided over the legal route to its outcome, even though Gregory and Thacker both rejected the requested injunction. The decision came from the Richmond-based Fourth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

The case is part of a broader disagreement among federal appeals courts about state power over prediction markets. The Third Circuit ruled for Kalshi and blocked New Jersey officials from applying state gambling restrictions to the exchange. The Ninth Circuit sided with Nevada, while the Sixth Circuit backed Ohio and Tennessee. The cited account counts federal appeals courts as having ruled against Kalshi’s effort to avoid state gambling regulation, and one as having ruled in its favor. Those counts describe appellate-court outcomes, not a final nationwide resolution of the underlying dispute.

New Jersey regulators have asked the Supreme Court to review the Third Circuit ruling, but the Court has not agreed to take the case. The cited reporting says little time remains in the current term for the Supreme Court to decide whether to accept it. If the Court does not act, a decision may not arrive until summer 2028. That possible timing concerns the pending request for Supreme Court review, not the outcome of Kalshi’s Maryland lawsuit. The reporting describes no Supreme Court decision to hear the New Jersey dispute, and Maryland has not stated whether it will pursue more enforcement.

The dispute matters to Kalshi and similar companies because they let users trade on outcomes that include sports and elections. States say such firms operate without licenses they require and breach gambling laws, including rules concerning users’ ages. Those state objections contrast with the CFTC’s position that prediction-market event contracts belong exclusively under its authority. Kalshi has said that opponents of prediction markets do not share a unified, coherent legal argument. Maryland’s acting lottery and gaming control commission director, Jeremy Baker, welcomed the decision as confirming state authority over sports wagering.

Other events involving Kalshi show that its markets have also drawn attention from the CFTC beyond the Maryland licensing dispute. After a CFTC order, Kalshi stopped offering wagers on whether Donald Trump would use particular words in speeches; the agency had called for the bets to end earlier. A White House teleprompter operator traded on markets concerning Trump’s remarks and received a ban from the platform. The operator also had to pay money and give up winnings to the CFTC. Separately, the CFTC put holds on certifications for some proposed Kalshi markets about mentions, including one initially self-certified, because the contracts could be vulnerable to manipulation, its spokesperson said.

Kalshi said it was valued at $40 billion in a recent funding round. Bloomberg Technology reported that the company was preparing to add stock trading to its app after acquiring a brokerage firm. Those developments sit alongside a legal dispute about whether state gambling rules apply to Kalshi’s sports contracts, rather than resolving that question. The Fourth Circuit ruling gives Maryland room to keep pursuing enforcement while the lawsuit continues, but leaves the underlying case undecided. With appeals courts reaching different results and the Supreme Court not yet agreeing to hear the New Jersey case, the national dispute remains unsettled in the cited reporting.

text:
The other day I met a hiring manager who only spoke in buzzwords. This man had somehow replaced his entire vocabulary with phrases stolen from a leadership retreat at a Marriott.

We sat down, and he said, “Before we deep dive, let’s circle back to your north star.” Sir, I just arrived. He wanted to “align on deliverables” before discussing the job. I asked what the position actually involved. He said, “Driving scalable synergies across cross-functional ecosystems.” Beautiful. So… nobody knows? I could have been interviewing to manage a warehouse, launch a spaceship, or supervise the office Keurig.

I asked what a typical day looked like. “We hit the ground running, move the needle, and leverage best practices.” Right. But doing WHAT? “We empower thought partners to operationalize strategic outcomes.” Was this an interview or a hostage video filmed by LinkedIn? My resume wanted out!! I swear one leaf fell off when he said “value proposition.”

Then he asked if I was comfortable wearing multiple hats. I said, “Sure, as long as one of them comes with a salary.” He laughed and said they needed someone who could “think outside the box while staying in their lane.” So you want innovation with a seat belt? A rebel who submits a permission slip? Got it. He nodded like I’d just unlocked the executive bonus level.

We moved to compensation. I asked for the salary range. He said, “We’re looking at a holistic rewards architecture.” I said, “Does the architecture have dollars in it?” Apparently they offer competitive compensation, an entrepreneurial mindset, and unlimited opportunities to make an impact. That’s three different ways to say the paycheck is hiding in witness protection. When I asked for a number again, he suggested we “take that offline.” WE ARE OFFLINE, GREG. THERE ARE TWO OF US IN A ROOM. Is payroll being stored in a different dimension?

Next came culture. “We’re a family here,” he announced. Of course. Every dysfunctional workplace has a family plan, and somehow it never includes dental. He promised radical transparency, then refused to answer how long the role had been open. “We’re navigating an exciting transformation.” Translation: six people quit, the copier is on fire, and someone named Kyle is temporarily handling four departments and a suspicious amount of crying.

At the end, he asked whether I had any questions. I did. “If we circle back to the low-hanging fruit, can we move the needle without boiling the ocean, or do we need to get all our ducks in a row before we take this to the next level?” His eyes lit up. He leaned forward and whispered, “Now you’re speaking my language.”

I left with no job description, no salary range, and a complimentary pen that said INNOVATE. Twenty minutes later, I received an email: “We’ve decided to pursue candidates whose competencies more closely align with our strategic roadmap.”

Translation: I asked what the job paid. But at least we built a bridge. Apparently it leads straight to nowhere.

Richard Anthony Proctor
23 March 1837 – 12 September 1888

English astronomer, mathematical investigator, celestial cartographer, scientific lecturer, author, and founding editor of Knowledge.

Proctor's documented credentials and intellectual accomplishments are more substantial than the abbreviated signatures on his title pages suggest.

• King's College London: Studied theology, receiving a B.A. in 1856.

• St John's College, Cambridge: Scholarship holder who studied mathematics and theology, graduating in 1860 as twenty-third Wrangler in the Mathematical Tripos.

• Royal Astronomical Society: Elected Fellow on 8 June 1866; subsequently served as honorary secretary beginning in 1872.

• Scientific publications: Authored 57 books and numerous astronomical research papers, including studies of stellar distribution, planetary rotations, solar prominences, and the transit of Venus.

• Celestial cartography: Charted 324,198 stars from Friedrich Argelander's northern stellar survey using an equal-surface projection.

• Independent investigations: Conducted mathematical work on cycloidal geometry, Mars's rotation, stellar and nebular distribution, and the constitution of the Milky Way.

• Scientific editorship: Founded Knowledge, the influential popular-science periodical, in 1881.

• Additional intellectual pursuits: Studied law, taught mathematics, devised astronomical illustrations, and was accomplished in chess, whist, and piano.

🔑 Specialist/Scholarly Pro-metary: The extraordinary ontological & Physical/Supernatural
